findings.finding: The opening says the team partly replicated the planning findings, names what the original found, and the abstract pairs representative successes with three changed threshold crossings and the extreme-setting rejection-rate discrepancy.

The first sentence says the headline findings partly replicated. The same paragraph describes fresh rather than replayed estimates, gives both main positive comparisons and exceptions, and precedes the background on page 2.
The text defines formulaic, exemplary and empirical power before interpreting them and explains the contrasts in prose. Evidence links and disagreement IDs supplement the explanation.
The distinct numerical and source regeneration routes are described with commands, scope and prerequisite pointers.

findings.location: Table 1, ICC row; compare p. 1 introduction and p. 2 section 2
findings.finding: Putting the published decline statement opposite only the rerun's .56 to .62 pp skew-size rebound reads as a source-versus-rerun disagreement. The introduction and section 2 report that the original Table 1 also has a rebound (.6098 to .6673 pp), so the page 1 headline row should explicitly attribute it on the published side while distinguishing it from the source prose.

A reader can trace the crossed grids, formulaic rules, planning contrasts, cluster thresholds, empirical/exemplary gap, Appendix C parameters and both Appendix D settings to distinct evidence. Completeness against the packet remains for the evidence phase.
The observed-count df extension, realized versus averaged mask estimands, and the proxy for unknown Appendix C source Monte Carlo errors are explicit.

The source software/fit state, masks, rates and interval procedure are characterized separately. The denominator sensitivity and adverse-mask checks are treated as plausible explanations, with discriminating original records identified.

The manuscript identifies which model, setting, targets and size schedules came from the dissertation and which extraction, generator reconstruction, independent checks and comparisons the replication performed.

findings.location: section 4, paired baseline and Appendix C paragraphs
findings.finding: The manuscript distinguishes fixed-covariance and refitted estimates on the same outcomes and explains why additional draws reduce uncertainty around each probability.

findings.location: subtitle and abstract opening; p. 12 reference
findings.finding: The subtitle identifies the longitudinal cluster trial study and the abstract attributes the findings to Kupzyk (2011). It states the loss ranking, lowest-ICC result, eight-cluster maximum and usual empirical deficit before reporting rerun outcomes. The references identify the exact dissertation.

findings.location: Table 1, signed effect, effect magnitude and direction columns, and note
findings.finding: The table lists both signed values for each of the eight rows, direction, relative magnitude, units/reference definitions, rounding tolerances and a separation from uncertainty and equivalence. The count row is terse, but the note defines the signed values 14 and 13 as counts above half the cells and Published/Ours shows the underlying 41 and 40 of 54.

findings.location: Table 1, Published and Ours cells in ICC row
findings.finding: The Published cell includes the stated decline and peak but omits the published table-derived skew-size rebound; only Ours describes a rebound. The paper's own numerical source finding on p. 2 makes the asymmetric presentation materially misleading.

findings.location: Table 1, loss, maximum count and below-count rows
findings.finding: The cells distinguish the published and reconstructed sides, report both values, and the note identifies the matched references, 0.5 integer tolerance and count origin. Evidence verification remains pending.
